title: Pilot passkeys for a workforce population
description: Enable passkeys for a bounded group of users on your primary identity provider, measure the enrollment and sign-in experience, and learn what recovery and support needs appear before wider rollout.
steps: Choose a pilot group and confirm supported devices and browsers
Enable passkey registration on the identity provider
Publish short enrollment and lost-device instructions
Collect support tickets and user feedback for one cycle
Decide on expansion criteria
successMetrics: Pilot users can enroll and sign in without help-desk assistance
Recovery path tested for a lost device
Documented list of blocking applications
dependencies: Identity provider that supports WebAuthn / passkeys

title: Design account recovery before removing passwords
description: Define and test how users regain access after losing every device, and ensure the recovery path is not weaker than the authenticator it replaces.
steps: Map current reset and recovery flows and their weaknesses
Define identity re-proofing requirements by risk level
Avoid knowledge-based questions as a recovery factor, since the personal data they rely on can be exposed in breaches
Add approval and notification steps for high-risk recovery
Run a tabletop test of a lost-device scenario
successMetrics: Recovery flow documented and tested
Recovery events are logged and reviewable

title: Assess identity maturity against a zero trust model
description: Score your identity capabilities against the CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model identity pillar to find the highest-value gaps and set a baseline for tracking progress.
steps: Read the identity pillar of the CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model
Workshop current capabilities with identity, network and endpoint owners
Record maturity stage per capability with evidence
Prioritize three gaps for the roadmap
successMetrics: Documented baseline with named owners
Gaps ranked and linked to roadmap items

title: Roll out context-aware access policies for key applications
description: Apply authentication strength and access conditions per application based on sensitivity, starting with the most critical applications and administrative portals.
steps: Classify applications by sensitivity
Define baseline policy tiers (authentication strength, device state, risk signals)
Run policies in report-only mode and review impact
Enforce tier by tier with exception handling
successMetrics: Critical applications covered by an explicit policy tier
Exceptions tracked with owners and expiry

title: Close identity logging gaps
description: Verify that identity provider, directory, PAM and cloud IAM logs reach your detection platform with enough detail to reconstruct authentication and privilege changes.
steps: List identity systems and their log sources
Confirm retention and ingestion for each source
Test that a known privilege change can be traced end to end
Document and ticket gaps
successMetrics: Each identity system has a verified log feed
A sample privilege change is traceable in the detection platform

title: Write identity incident response playbooks
description: Create tested playbooks for compromised accounts, suspicious privilege grants and session hijacking, including who can disable accounts and revoke sessions and tokens.
steps: Select scenarios from observed or ATT&CK-mapped identity techniques
Define containment actions and approvers
Automate low-risk steps such as session revocation where feasible
Exercise each playbook and record lessons
successMetrics: Playbooks exist and have been exercised
Containment authority is documented

title: Build an owned inventory of non-human identities
description: Discover service accounts, API keys, tokens and workload identities, assign a named owner and purpose to each, and flag those that are unused, over-privileged or long-lived.
steps: Pull accounts and credentials from directories, cloud IAM and secret stores
Assign an owner and purpose to each identity
Flag unused, shared and long-lived credentials
Set a policy for creating new non-human identities
successMetrics: Every inventoried identity has a named owner
Orphaned identities identified and scheduled for removal

title: Move workloads to short-lived credentials
description: Replace static secrets with federated or attested, short-lived credentials where platforms allow, and rotate the remainder on a defined schedule.
steps: Prioritize workloads holding the most sensitive static secrets
Adopt workload identity federation or attestation for those workloads
Automate rotation for secrets that cannot be removed
Block creation of new long-lived keys where possible
successMetrics: Number of static long-lived credentials trends downward
Rotation is automated for remaining secrets

title: Fix the authoritative source for joiners, movers and leavers
description: Establish a trusted HR-driven source of identity lifecycle events and measure how quickly access changes follow, before layering on advanced governance features.
steps: Document the current lifecycle data flow from HR to systems
Identify data quality defects such as missing managers or stale statuses
Define mover and leaver triggers and expected timelines
Measure and report lifecycle timeliness
successMetrics: Leaver access removal timeliness is measured
Data quality defects are tracked to closure

title: Shift access reviews to risk-based certification
description: Focus reviewer effort on high-risk entitlements and unusual access, and reduce or automate review of low-risk, well-governed access to limit review fatigue.
steps: Classify entitlements by risk
Define review frequency and reviewer by risk tier
Provide reviewers with usage and peer-group context
Compare review outcomes before and after the change
successMetrics: Reviewers can explain decisions for high-risk entitlements
Revocation rate for high-risk items is tracked

title: Reduce standing administrator access
description: Inventory permanent privileged role assignments and convert them to eligible, time-bound elevation for the most sensitive roles first.
steps: List permanent privileged assignments across directories and cloud
Remove assignments that are unused or unjustified
Convert remaining sensitive roles to eligible, time-bound access
Require approval or justification for the highest-risk roles
successMetrics: Standing privileged assignments are justified and owned
Elevation events are logged with a reason

title: Harden and test emergency access accounts
description: Ensure break-glass accounts exist, are strongly protected, are not dependent on the systems they are meant to recover, and trigger alerts when used.
steps: Identify existing emergency accounts
Protect credentials with strong, offline-recoverable authentication
Alert on every use
Test the procedure on a schedule
successMetrics: Emergency access is tested and any use is alerted
Credential custody is documented

title: Review unused and external-access findings in cloud IAM
description: Use provider-native analyzers to list unused permissions and unintended external access, then remediate the highest-risk findings with owners.
steps: Enable the provider's access analysis features
Triage findings by resource sensitivity
Assign remediation to account owners
Track findings to closure
successMetrics: High-risk findings have an owner and due date
Closed findings are verified

title: Embed least-privilege checks in infrastructure-as-code pipelines
description: Check proposed IAM policies for excessive permissions before deployment, so new access is right-sized at creation instead of corrected later.
steps: Select a policy-validation tool supported by your cloud provider
Add checks to pull requests for IAM changes
Define what blocks a merge versus what warns
Review exceptions regularly
successMetrics: IAM changes pass automated checks before deployment
Exception list is small and reviewed

title: Assess where verifiable credentials could help
description: Identify one or two processes such as onboarding, partner access or credential verification where reusable credentials could reduce friction, and document the trust and privacy requirements.
steps: Collect candidate use cases with business owners
Identify who would issue, hold and verify the credentials
Assess regulatory and privacy constraints
Select at most one use case for a pilot decision
successMetrics: Use cases documented with issuers and verifiers named
Go or no-go decision recorded

title: Track digital identity wallet requirements for your sector
description: Monitor wallet and trust framework developments that may affect customer or employee onboarding, and plan how your relying-party systems would accept wallet credentials.
steps: Assign an owner to track regulatory and standards changes
Review which journeys might accept wallet credentials
Identify technical changes needed to verify credentials
Revisit the plan on each dataset review
successMetrics: Named owner and review cadence
Documented list of affected journeys

title: Inventory AI agents and the credentials they use
description: Find out which AI agents and assistants act in your environment, which identities and tokens they use, and what they can reach, before writing policy.
steps: Survey teams for agents, assistants and automation using AI models
Record the credentials, scopes and data each can access
Identify agents acting with a shared or human user's credentials
Name an owner for each agent
successMetrics: Each known agent has an owner and a credential record
Agents using shared human credentials are identified

title: Require scoped, short-lived delegation for agents
description: Set a standard that agents act with narrowly scoped, expiring, auditable credentials tied to the delegating user and task, and require human approval for high-impact actions.
steps: Define allowed scopes and token lifetimes for agents
Require the delegating user to be recorded in audit logs
Identify actions that need human approval
Review current specifications and update the standard as they evolve
successMetrics: Agent actions are attributable to an agent and a delegating user
High-impact actions require approval

title: Map identity obligations to your regulatory scope
description: With legal and compliance, list which regulations apply to your entities and extract the identity and access requirements they imply, with citations to the official text.
steps: Confirm applicable regulations by entity and jurisdiction
Extract identity-related obligations with references
Map obligations to existing controls
Record gaps and owners
successMetrics: Obligation-to-control map exists with citations
Gaps have owners

title: Automate evidence collection for access controls
description: Generate recurring evidence of authentication strength, access reviews and privileged access directly from systems so audits do not depend on manual screenshots.
steps: List evidence requests auditors ask for most often
Identify the system of record for each
Schedule exports or reports with integrity controls
Review the evidence pack with auditors
successMetrics: Evidence for key controls is produced on a schedule
Audit requests are answered from system reports
